title: Potato from Puerto Rican style stuffed pot roast, with gravy

content.title: About
content.content: This dish features a large potato baked until tender, stuffed with cubes of pot‑roast seasoned in a Puerto Rican style, and served with a rich gravy. The combination of creamy potato, juicy meat and aromatic sauce delivers a taste of the Caribbean.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Stuffing potatoes with meat dates back to Spanish colonies in the Caribbean.
Puerto Rican seasoning often includes adobo, oregano, garlic and lime, giving the dish its distinctive aroma.
The pot‑roast is usually cooked ahead of time and diced finely for even distribution inside the potato.
The gravy is made from chicken stock, cream and a touch of tomato paste, resulting in a thick, velvety sauce.
The dish is commonly served with fried plantains or rice and beans, staples of Puerto Rican cuisine.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Potato provides sustained energy thanks to its high starch content.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and muscle function.

items.title: Protein from pot‑roast
items.content: The meat adds complete protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Puerto Rican spices such as oregano and garlic contain antioxidants that combat free radicals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The gravy can be salty; people with hypertension should watch portion size.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: If the gravy is thickened with wheat flour, it may pose a problem for those with celiac disease.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: Pot‑roast contains saturated fat; moderate consumption is advised for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Risk of overeating
items.content: The dish is calorie‑dense, so portions should be controlled, especially on weight‑loss plans.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot, cutting the potato in half and spooning the stuffing inside. Garnish with fresh herbs, a squeeze of lime, or a dash of hot sauce for extra zing. It pairs well with rice, beans or fried plantains.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool leftovers to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat in the oven to retain the potato’s crisp skin.
